our_side: Three seats on the east strip from lobby seats on side Random: t1 G1 Armada (ai 0), t2 H8 Cortex (ai 1), t3 G4 Cortex (ai 2). One player, claude-opus-5-5 effort medium (Claude Code 2.1.283), over all three seats, no commander; hands Jev jev-1.13.0 per seat (jev-latest); packet decompression on (packet_rules); realtime. summary: Three Opus-run seats (t1 Armada at G1, t2 and t3 Cortex at H8 and G4) against thebluegecko on Comet, with Irishstud14 spectating and advising in chat. The Cortex seats' opening lists were all refused (the tools knew the lead seat's Armada roster only), yet the side held 34 extractors at income 102 by 10:45, and t2+t3's Thug ball broke his D3/D4 outpost by 10:18 while the packet kept t1's ground army at home at F2; from 11:05 the ball met his Stout-and-Janus blocks one group at a time at C3, D4 and E4. Counting each death once, the trade was even to 14:00 (12.8k lost to 13.1k destroyed), but the player's report summed the three seats and read about 3:1 in our favour all game. From 14:14 his Banshees (no anti-air of ours until 15:13), then Mausers firing from out of sight (16:23) and Bulls (18:21) beat a tier-1 army that never went tier 2 and never saw his base; our commanders died at 22:12 and 24:08, and t1's self-destructed at about 26:13 when a spectator suggested it. Irishstud14 at 15:06: "red not moblizing fast enough is what lost you the game".

root.what: The player split the side: t2+t3 were 'the ball' and t1's ground army (26 Pawns and Maces, 1.6-2.9k) stayed home 'guarding our northern extractors from spot_16' (said again at 8:48 and 9:32). t1's group then held at F2 from about 9:00 to 13:40. t3 reached C3 alone at 11:05 and t2 fed itself in a trickle at D4/E4 until 14:00, so his blocks never met the three armies at once. The person (Irishstud14) gives the same cause; red = t1 is our reading.
root.evidence: 7:54 note: 't2+t3 Grunt/Thug groups (3.6k) advance together to spot_33 ... t1 Pawns + turrets + commanders guard home'; 13:26 report: 'group_A_t1 ... 31 soldiers worth 2629 metal; at spot_16 (F2); holding for 271 s'; Irishstud14 15:06 'red not moblizing fast enough is what lost you the game'

our_mistakes.what: The root: t1's ground army was kept home while two seats pushed, and the push went without one gathering place. A stronger side brings all three armies to one place and goes together (Irishstud14 13:20-17:46). t1's 2.0-2.9k joining the even fights at D4/E4 was the cheapest swing available.
our_mistakes.evidence: 8:48 and 9:32 packets 'group_A_t1 guards our northern extractors from spot_16'; minutes seat 0 our mass F2 at 0-7% in his half every minute; Irishstud14 14:00 'red really needs to use his ground troops'

our_mistakes.what: The Grunts (fast) ran ahead of the Thugs into a turret outpost and 23 died without effect. A stronger player keeps the fast units with the body, or sends the Thugs first against the LLTs and Beamer.
our_mistakes.evidence: minutes seats 1-2: 23 corak dead at D3/E3 8:23-9:25 to armllt/armbeamer/armflash; seat 0 #5 shows the outpost fell only to the Thugs 9:16-10:18

our_mistakes.what: On Irishstud14's 'you have enough E' the player set `constructors solar: never` for the side until 16:15. t2 built no solar from 6:31 to 17:09 and stalled its energy in minutes 10-18, with 1.5-1.9k metal banked from 11:00 to 21:00. t3 built 25 converters on a metal map. A stronger player keeps energy rising with income (200+ a second, nanos) and spends the bank.
our_mistakes.evidence: commander_turns 6:39 standing {constructors: {solar: never}}; 16:15 {solar: freely}; floor seat 1 e0% 34.1, mfull% 35.8; analyze seat 1 bank 1515-1997 at 11:00-14:00; Irishstud14 16:14 'yellow and orange need more energy'

Next came Stout-and-Janus blocks with artillery behind (from 9:40), holding C3/D4 and trading about even against the seats one group at a time (he lost 5,490 at D4 from 11:34 to 13:17). The Bulls raided t2's home (21:00-22:12) and t3's (23:50-24:08), and a Razorback came at 25:15. His factories were never seen. From 14:00 every fight was in our half: 23,275 of the 37,058 metal of his we saw die died there.

bears_on.note: This game is the lesson's source. t1's group held at F2 for about 4.75 minutes (9:00-13:40) while t3 met his block alone at C3 (11:05) and t2 fed in a stream at D4/E4; the even fights there were the place a third army would have counted.
This game is the source. At 6:34 we chose bombers over tier 2 and never teched in a 3v1 with 1.5-2k banked; his Mausers (16:23) and Bulls (18:21) decided the second half.

First construction turrets at 16:17/19:36/19:59; t2's energy was empty 34% of the game with its metal store full 36%, and the side's solars were stopped 6:39-16:15 on a misapplied 'you have enough E'.
The wreck fields at D3/D4 (11:41 'get that reclaim asap'); later wakes said 5.7k-10.7k of wrecks lay unworked; two Lazarus at 10:15-10:38 and four Graves only from 17:21.
11 exit-lane wakes and 357-522 s of stuck units per seat; the player's 13:53 guess 'labs clutter E4?'.
t3 built 25 converters from 5:19 (t1 15) on a metal map, while t2 starved of energy; the line was said two games later.
Our first soldier in his half crossed at 6:48 (the pool's Armada median 1:40); he raided us from 2:31 while his own extractors were never touched before the D3 outpost fell at 9:16-10:18.
It bounds the lesson: the lead the player 'used' was a seen floor (9.4k against ~1k seen) and a triple-counted trade; counted once, the trade was level at 11:00.
Our reading: an all-Thug ground mass with no anti-air left him safe to go air at 14:14 and tier 2 by 16:23.

lens.caveats: No truth file and no results.jsonl/batch.json: his numbers are seen floors and HIS TIER 2 is empty. Every per-match tool reads record-0 only, so seats 1-2 ran through scratchpad symlinks. pro_baseline's pool is 1v1 duels (none from G1/B8 as Armada, so --all-starts), a weak yardstick per seat in a 3v1. raid_ledger reads 'answer none' for all, since its regex cuts party_46_t2. chat.jsonl gives every speaker as '?': I attributed by player id, following lessons.md for Irishstud14, and separated the host's lines by the transcript's say calls. That red = t1 is our reading (the player read it so; the numbers fit). minutes.py's first window (6:00-7:00, 0% in his half) rests on a seen floor while the true trade at 6:00 was against us, so I placed the root at the 7:54 split the person names.
